clue.text: Company minutes assure accommodation

parts.note: to assure someone is to promise them

explanation.surface: A firm's record of a meeting guarantees there was an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: An accommodation is a settlement in which both sides give ground, a mutual concession.

clue.text: Scratch copyright code of conduct

parts.note: C, as in the copyright symbol
a law is a rule or code governing conduct

explanation.surface: Someone scraps the copyright rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratch' suggests deleting or cancelling, but it is the definition: to scratch with nails.
explanation.definitionFit: To claw is to scratch or tear with nails or talons.

clue.text: Aircraft designers apportion movement from one part to another

definitions.text: movement from one part to another

parts.note: MiG is the Russian design bureau of Mikoyan and Gurevich, makers of fighter jets
to ration is to apportion or share out in fixed amounts

explanation.surface: Aircraft engineers share out the transfer of parts between places.
explanation.definitionFit: Migration is the movement of people or animals from one region to another.

clue.text: Agitated, turning up lightheaded, without promissory notes

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the letters read bottom to top, backwards
without means the following letters are taken away from the previous word

parts.note: lightheaded can mean dizzy and confused, delirious
IOUs are promissory notes, written promises to pay

explanation.surface: Someone is dizzy and upset, with no IOUs to their name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops IOUS from DELIRIOUS, leaving DELIR, which 'turning up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Riled means annoyed or irritated, a state of being agitated.

clue.text: Flaming thing Sheeran made harmonious

parts.note: a match is a thing that flames when struck
Ed Sheeran is a British pop singer

explanation.surface: A singer is said to have set his songs alight and made them tuneful.
explanation.definitionFit: To match colours or items is to make them go together well, so harmonious pairing is matching.

clue.text: Detergent's bogus power over heart of pathogens

parts.note: a sham is something bogus or fake
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: heart of takes the central letter of the word pathogens

explanation.surface: A cleaning product's claimed germ-killing strength is a fake.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link (is). An over is a set of six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is a liquid cleanser for hair or carpets, a kind of detergent.

clue.text: Bluster about wrangle

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
a wrangle is a row, a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: Someone blusters their way around an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To bluster is to boast loudly, which is what to crow means as a verb.

clue.text: Predominance of downpours we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals that the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: downpours are heavy falls of rain

explanation.surface: Heavy showers dominate, according to the forecast.
explanation.definitionFit: A reign is a period of rule or dominance, so predominance fits.

clue.text: Motor part engineer screwed in with nitrogen

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or rework, so the letters of screwed in are rearranged

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A mechanic screws in a car component using nitrogen.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor is a car, and the glass at its front is one of its parts.

clue.text: Measure of revolutionary network supporting upset servant

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the other
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a maid is a servant

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the word for network is reversed

parts.note: a rete is an anatomical network of nerves or vessels

explanation.surface: A radical system holds up an overturned servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns MAID into DIAM; 'revolutionary' turns RETE into ETER, which goes under it.
explanation.definitionFit: The diameter is a measurement, the width across a circle through its centre.

clue.text: Historically, coin article on support from the Right

parts.note: AN is the indefinite article

indicators.note: read from the right, i.e. the word for support is written backwards

parts.note: a leg is a support, as of a table

explanation.surface: An old coin is described as sitting on a stand, viewed from the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the Right' means read right to left; 'on' is a link joining the article to what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The angel was an old English gold coin showing the archangel Michael, so it is a coin of the past.

clue.text: Custom of resolved administrator ditching defective arms

indicators.note: resolved means broken down and reworked, so the letters of administrator are rearranged
ditching means the letters of the second word are thrown out of that pool
defective arms are faulty, so the word arms is jumbled before it is removed

parts.note: used as written for its letters
used as written for its letters

explanation.surface: An administrator who has made up their mind gets rid of faulty weapons, which is apparently customary.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a composite anagram: the letters of ADMINISTRATOR, less the letters A, R, M, S, rearrange to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom is a practice handed down over time, an established tradition-bearing habit; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Rigorous internet protocol limiting daughter's misfortune

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing, so the first pieces hold the next

parts.note: rigorous conditions are harsh ones

explanation.surface: Strict internet rules are blamed for a daughter's bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limiting' puts D inside HARSHIP, splitting it after HAR. The 's is a link (has).
explanation.definitionFit: Misfortune means suffering or adversity, which is what a hardship is.

clue.text: Short of money at first on other side of Atlantic

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word money

parts.note: on the other side of the Atlantic, seen from Britain, is in the US

explanation.surface: Someone is low on cash early on while across the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Minus can mean lacking or without, as in arriving minus a coat, the same as short of.

clue.text: Pass over poll, lacking energy for gathering input

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

indicators.note: lacking means the following letter is missing from the word for poll

parts.note: a poll is an election

explanation.surface: Someone skips a vote, too tired to collect contributions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking energy' drops one E from ELECTION, leaving LECTION. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection is a gathering of contributions, such as money taken in at church.

clue.text: Old hand editor left out

parts.note: mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: A veteran editor was excluded from something.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left out has been excluded or skipped, a straight synonym.

clue.text: State department judge ensnaring a user wrongly

indicators.note: ensnaring means trapping inside, so the word for judge surrounds the rest

parts.note: to try a case is to judge it

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters of a user are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A judge catches someone misusing government services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ensnaring' places the anagram, made by 'wrongly', between the R and Y of the word for judge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Treasury is the government department that manages a state's finances.

clue.text: Perform better than form, essentially, away from house

parts.note: to outdo someone is to perform better than them

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the central letters of the word form

explanation.surface: Someone excels at form, preferably out of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoor activities happen in the open air, not inside a building.

clue.text: Players with excited roar about 16, say

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jumbled letters surround the next piece
excited means stirred up, so the letters of roar are mixed

parts.note: a treasury (the answer to 16 Down) can be a chest, a store of funds; say marks this as an example

explanation.surface: Performers roar with excitement about a state department.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 16 needs that answer first: a treasury can be a strongbox or chest of funds, and 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a group of musicians, that is, players.

clue.text: Type of light lake punt associated with Royal Navy

parts.note: a punt is a bet, and an ante is a stake put up before the deal in poker

explanation.surface: A punt on a lake is linked to the navy, like a light boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' looks like the flat-bottomed boat but here means a gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp with a protective case, a kind of light.

clue.text: Yellowish brown rising Russian river's not abnormal

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: tan is a yellowish brown colour
the Ural is a river flowing through Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: A brownish Russian river swelling is quite normal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something natural is normal and as expected, the opposite of abnormal.

clue.text: Listener's problem; endlessly hears fact she'd gathered

indicators.note: endlessly strips the first and last letters from each of the three words, keeping their centres

explanation.surface: Someone hears a fact that she had collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered' is a link: the three cores are gathered into one word. The apostrophe in she'd is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A listener uses their ears, so pain in the ear is a problem for a listener.

clue.text: Feature of laciest pants?

indicators.note: pants as a verb is unused; read as British slang for rubbish, it signals the letters of laciest are scrambled

explanation.surface: A question about what the frilliest knickers have.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English 'pants' are underpants, and also slang for poor, which signals the anagram. The whole clue is also the definition: underwear has a stretchy waistband.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretchy elastic in the waistband is a standard feature of underpants.

clue.text: Clunkiest shabby knit dropped revealing these

indicators.note: shabby suggests something worn and out of shape, so the letters of Clunkiest are jumbled
dropped means the letters of the word knit fall out of that pool

parts.note: used as written for its letters
used as written for its letters

explanation.walkthrough: 'knit dropped' suggests dropped stitches; in fact K, N, I, T leave CLUNKIEST to give the answer. 'these' points at the very things the solver is reading.

clue.text: Unshackle the BBC, sacking staff essentially

indicators.note: sacking means dismissing, so the next letter is removed

parts.note: Auntie, or Auntie Beeb, is a British nickname for the BBC

indicators.note: essentially takes the central letter of the word staff

explanation.walkthrough: AUNTIE (the British public broadcaster's nickname) loses A, the middle of STAFF.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie is to release from bonds, which is what unshackle means.

clue.text: Umpire's new skill going west in change of club?

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means reading right to left, backwards

parts.note: an umpire is a referee, REF, and the 's adds S
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.walkthrough: 'going west' reverses REFSNART. The question mark flags that a footballer's change of club is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: When a footballer moves from one club to another, the deal is called a transfer.

clue.text: Scour stunted trees and bushes

definitions.meaning: to scour is to clean by hard rubbing
low, stunted vegetation covering rough ground

explanation.definitionFit: To scrub is to rub clean, and scrub is also land covered with low bushes.

clue.text: Temporary state of mounting catastrophe

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means climbing, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: doom is a terrible fate, a catastrophe

explanation.surface: A passing condition of growing disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A mood is a passing frame of mind, a temporary emotional condition.

clue.text: Understand concern, not small, about public relations

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened word goes round the next piece
not here removes a letter from the word for concern

parts.note: a concern is an interest, as in having a stake in something

explanation.walkthrough: 'not small' drops S from INTEREST to give INTERET, which goes 'about' PR.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret something is to work out its meaning, which is to understand it.

clue.text: Part of administration's relative magnitude

indicators.note: part of means the letters lie within the word administration's

explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses how large one quantity is compared with another.

clue.text: Desire once held disappears now and then

indicators.note: every other letter of once held vanishes, leaving the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A longing that was once felt fades away from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: A need is a want or requirement, which is what desire means here.

clue.text: Support management acquiring large classroom item

indicators.note: acquiring means taking something in, so the word for support holds the next letter

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
